Add about 50 ml of distilled water to the beaker using the wash bottle to begin dissolving the powder. Use the stream to rinse the beaker walls.
Now, carefully pour the dissolved sodium carbonate solution from the beaker into the 250 ml volumetric flask. Ensure you don't spill any liquid during the transfer.
Continue filling the flask with distilled water. Watch the graduation mark on the neck closely; this indicates your final target volume of 250 ml.
Finally, place the glass stopper on the flask and invert it several times to mix the solution thoroughly until it is completely homogeneous.

question: I'm installing a Z-Wave add-on switch and following this tutorial. Please guide me through the process step by step as it unfolds.
event: I'm installing a Z-Wave add-on switch and following this tutorial. Please guide me through the process step by step as it unfolds.

ground_truth.response: First, ensure your safety by turning off the power at the circuit breaker or fuse box before beginning any electrical work.
Now, remove the wall plates from both switch locations by unscrewing the small screws with a manual screwdriver.
Use a power drill to remove the mounting screws, then carefully pull the old switches out of the wall boxes without disconnecting any wires.
Turn the power back on. Use a multimeter to test the black common screw on each switch; the one showing power is your primary line switch.
Turn the power off again. Label the black wire on the primary switch as 'Line' and the black wire on the other switch as 'Load'.
Next, use a manual screwdriver to disconnect all the wires from both of the old toggle switches.
Locate the white neutral wire bundle in the back of the box. Add a white splice wire to the bundle and secure it with a wire nut.
Connect the white neutral splice wire to the silver terminal, the labeled 'Line' wire to the black terminal, and the ground wire to the green terminal.
Connect the black traveler wire to the load terminal and the red traveler wire to the gold terminal on the primary switch.
In the second box, create another neutral splice and connect it to the silver terminal of the add-on switch. Also, connect the ground wire to the green terminal.
Join the 'Load' wire and the black traveler wire together with a wire nut. Then, connect the red traveler wire to the gold terminal on the add-on switch.
Tuck the wires back into the boxes and secure both switches to the wall using the long mounting screws and your drill.
Place the wall plates over the switches and tighten the small screws to complete the physical installation.
